title: Loan Against Mutual Funds Interest Rate: What You'll Actually Pay at Yenmo
summary: The interest rate on a loan against mutual funds at Yenmo is 9.89% to 10.49% a year, set by your sanctioned amount. See the slabs and the cost in rupees.
body_markdown:
*By Ashutosh Purohit*


You've seen a rate like "from 9.89%" and you want to know what it means for your own loan. At Yenmo, the interest rate on a loan against mutual funds is 9.89% to 10.49% a year, and your rate is set by the size of your sanctioned limit. Interest is charged only on the amount you withdraw, so every ₹1 lakh you take out costs about ₹824 to ₹874 a month.


**The short version**


- Your rate depends on your sanctioned amount. It runs from 10.49% a year on the smallest loans to 9.89% on ₹2 crore and above.
- No loan at Yenmo is priced over 10.49% a year.
- Interest runs only on money you've withdrawn, and there's no EMI.
- Repaying early costs ₹0, so you can stop the interest on any day you have the money.


## What is the interest rate on a loan against mutual funds at Yenmo?


It is between 9.89% and 10.49% a year. The loan is a 3-year credit line, which means a lender sanctions a limit against your pledged funds and you withdraw from it when you need money. The size of that limit decides your rate.


Sanctioned amount Interest rate (a year) Interest on each ₹1 lakh withdrawn, per month


₹2 crore and above 9.89% About ₹824


₹1 crore – ₹2 crore 9.99% About ₹833


₹50 lakh – ₹1 crore 10.09% About ₹841


₹25 lakh – ₹50 lakh 10.19% About ₹849


₹10 lakh – ₹25 lakh 10.29% About ₹858


₹2 lakh – ₹10 lakh 10.39% About ₹866


₹25,000 – ₹2 lakh 10.49% About ₹874


These are the slabs for loans from Bajaj Finance, one of our lending partners. DSP Finance also lends through Yenmo.


The gap between the first slab and the last is 0.60 percentage points. On ₹1 lakh withdrawn for a full year, that is a difference of ₹600. So the slab matters less than two things you control, which are how much you withdraw and how long you keep it.


## Which amount sets your rate?


The sanctioned amount sets it, and that is not always the amount you withdraw.


The sanctioned amount is the most the lender has agreed to lend you. What you can withdraw on a given day is the value of your pledged funds multiplied by the loan-to-value ratio, or LTV. Through Yenmo, Bajaj Finance lends 50% of the value of equity funds, up to 90% of liquid funds and typically 70% to 80% of other debt funds.


Some people ask for a sanction above what they can withdraw today, because they plan to pledge more funds later. Say you have ₹1 crore of equity funds. You can withdraw up to ₹50 lakh, but you take a ₹60 lakh sanction because you'll add ₹20 lakh of funds next year. Your rate comes from the ₹60 lakh, so you pay 10.09% a year and not 10.19%.


Withdrawing less doesn't change the slab either. If your sanction is ₹12 lakh and you take out only ₹1 lakh, you still pay 10.29% on that ₹1 lakh.


## How is the interest charged?


Interest is charged only on the amount you've withdrawn, not on your full limit. The part of the limit you haven't used costs you nothing in interest.


There's no EMI. You pay the interest each month, and you repay the amount itself when you choose. You can repay in parts or all at once, and interest stops on whatever you've repaid.


The smallest withdrawal is ₹500. So if you need ₹40,000 this month and ₹60,000 two months later, take them separately. The second amount costs nothing until the day you withdraw it.


## A worked example


Say Meera is a doctor in Indore with ₹12 lakh in equity funds. Her clinic needs equipment worth ₹3 lakh, and she expects to pay it back from her income in four months.


At 50% LTV, her funds give her a limit of ₹6 lakh. A ₹6 lakh sanction falls in the ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh slab, so her rate is 10.39% a year.


- She withdraws ₹3 lakh. Interest for one month is ₹3,00,000 × 10.39% ÷ 12, which comes to about ₹2,598.
- She keeps the money for four months, so her total interest is about ₹10,390.
- She pays the processing fee once. It starts from ₹1,649 + GST.
- At the end of month four she repays the ₹3 lakh, and closing early costs her ₹0.


Now change one thing. A patient's insurance claim comes through early, and she repays ₹1.5 lakh after two months. The interest for the last two months halves, and her total falls to about ₹7,793.


If interest had been charged on her full ₹6 lakh limit, the same four months would have cost ₹20,780. She paid half of that because she used half the limit.


These are rounded monthly figures, and your loan statement shows the exact interest. You can try your own numbers on the[loan against mutual fund calculator](https://yenmo.in/calculators/loan-against-mutual-fund-calculator) .


## What else do you pay besides interest?


You pay a processing fee once, from ₹1,649 + GST. It is the same whatever your sanctioned limit, and on Bajaj Finance loans it covers stamp duty and your first pledge and unpledge.


Bajaj Finance loans through Yenmo have no annual fee and no renewal fee during the 3 years. Repaying part of the loan or all of it early is free.


Lenders also have smaller charges, such as a fee for pledging more funds later or a penal charge for a missed payment. We list all of them on our[charges page](https://yenmo.in/charges) , with a tab for each lender. Read the tab for your lender before you apply.


When the 3 years end, you either close the loan or renew it for another 3 years by paying the processing fee again.


## What should you watch out for?


Interest adds up with time. At 10.39%, ₹3 lakh kept for a full year costs ₹31,170 in interest, and three years cost ₹93,510. A loan against mutual funds works well when you need money for a few months and don't want to sell. If you'd keep the money out for years, compare the interest with what your funds are likely to earn.


The second risk is a market fall. Your limit is tied to the current value of your pledged funds, so it drops when fund prices drop. Bajaj Finance compares that limit with the amount you've withdrawn.


If the limit falls to 90% of what you've withdrawn, you get 7 business days to repay part of it or pledge more funds. Below 85%, Bajaj sells pledged funds straight away and informs you.


Meera withdrew ₹3 lakh against ₹12 lakh of funds. Her funds would have to fall by 55%, to ₹5.4 lakh, before she was asked to top up. Had she withdrawn the full ₹6 lakh, a 10% fall would have been enough. Our post on[what happens if your mutual funds fall after you take a loan](https://yenmo.in/blog/what-happens-if-mutual-fund-value-falls-after-loan) explains this with more examples.


## How do you check your own rate?


Start the eligibility check on the[loan against mutual funds](https://yenmo.in/products/loan-against-mutual-funds) page with the mobile number linked to your investments. It shows the limit you can get, and the table above tells you the rate for that limit.


You'll need your PAN, Aadhaar for KYC and a bank account, and there's no minimum credit score. For funds held with CAMS or KFintech, the application takes about 5 to 7 minutes. If you want to know how the limit is worked out first, read[how much you can borrow against mutual funds](https://yenmo.in/blog/how-much-can-you-borrow-against-mutual-funds) .


Checking costs nothing, and interest starts only on the day you withdraw.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the interest rate on a loan against mutual funds at Yenmo?


It is 9.89% to 10.49% a year, set by your sanctioned amount. Loans of ₹25,000 to ₹2 lakh are at 10.49%, and the rate steps down to 9.89% for ₹2 crore and above. No loan at Yenmo is priced over 10.49% a year.


### Is interest charged on the full limit or only on what I withdraw?


Only on what you withdraw. If your limit is ₹6 lakh and you take out ₹3 lakh, you pay interest on ₹3 lakh. The unused part of the limit carries no interest.


### How much interest will I pay on ₹1 lakh?


About ₹824 to ₹874 a month, depending on your rate slab. At 10.39% a year, which applies to sanctioned amounts of ₹2 lakh to ₹10 lakh, ₹1 lakh costs about ₹866 a month for as long as you keep it.


### Does my rate change if I withdraw less than my limit?


No. The rate is set by the sanctioned amount, not by how much of it you use. Withdrawing less lowers the interest you pay in rupees, but the rate stays the same.


### Do I have to pay an EMI?


No. You pay only the interest each month on the amount you've withdrawn. You repay the amount itself in parts or in full whenever you like during the 3-year credit line.


### Is there a charge for repaying early?


No. Part-payment, prepayment and foreclosure all cost ₹0 at Yenmo. Interest stops on the amount you repay, so paying back early is the simplest way to cut your cost.
